guard: One private Linux file take releases bounded bytes only from a held, private directory and consumes its name
why: The public source export runs against real private files and child processes. A labelled parent-rename filesystem interleaving proves held-directory custody; the FIFO reader has an external owned-process deadline so removing O_NONBLOCK yields a named failure rather than an ungraded suite hang. No broker, document authentication, environment admission or manager bootstrap is claimed. Source imports read the changed module directly, leaving no compiled mutant artifacts.

mutations.expectRed: unlink and directory sync precede the first byte read
mutations.cell: unlink and directory sync precede the first byte read

mutations.name: take follows the mutable parent pathname instead of its held descriptor
mutations.expectRed: a parent rename cannot redirect the held deletion or read
mutations.cell: a parent rename cannot redirect the held deletion or read
